segments.sensitive: Reports from reviewers with sensitive skin are sharply split: some say it's gentle enough for very sensitive or acne-prone sensitive skin, but several others describe burning, hives, a rash, or a broken skin barrier, and two reviewers who say they do NOT have sensitive skin also report chemical burns and stripped, painful skin.
segments.dry: The reviewers who describe dry skin say it works without irritation, though one notes her skin feels a bit tight afterward and needs a good moisturizer to follow.
segments.oily: Most reviewers with oily skin say it controls oil without over-drying and call it one of the best cleansers for oily, acne-prone skin, but a couple of reviewers with oily skin report it stripped and dried their skin more than anything they'd tried before.
segments.combination: Most reviewers with combination skin report it works well without drying them out, focusing use on oilier areas, but one reviewer with combination skin says it left her skin dry, flaky, and peeling after just a few days, which she believed was an allergic reaction.
segments.normal: The one reviewer who describes normal skin says the cleanser worked on stubborn acne where nothing else had, though it was a little drying and needed a moisturizer to offset that.

concerns.dehydration: Reviewers are sharply divided: a large number say the cleanser is non-drying or even hydrating, while a comparable number report significant dryness, tightness, flaking, or peeling, some so severe it happened within days regardless of their skin type; several who found it drying recommend using it fewer times per week or always following with a rich moisturizer.
concerns.redness: Several reviewers say the cleanser calmed pre-existing redness thanks to the cica or cucumber in the formula, one noting only a brief five-minute flush after rinsing; but multiple other reviewers report the opposite — new redness, inflammation, or soreness appearing after use.
concerns.barrier: Three reviewers specifically describe the cleanser as having damaged or broken their skin barrier, reporting facial burning, stinging, and an altered skin texture that persisted after stopping use.
concerns.spots: One reviewer says her pigmentation is starting to fade with use, though another says the cleanser controlled her acne but did not clear the dark spots and blemish marks she was hoping to fade.
concerns.blemishes: The large majority of reviewers say the cleanser noticeably reduced acne, blackheads, or pimples within days to weeks, and a few reviewers explain that an initial purge of small bumps in the first few weeks is normal for a salicylic-acid product and resolves on its own; still, several other reviewers report the opposite — a worse or new breakout, in a few cases cystic, that only cleared once they stopped using it.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers with oily skin say the cleanser cuts oil and shine through the day without stripping their skin, several specifically using it to target oilier areas like the T-zone.

This cleanser made monumental improvements to my skin! I am truly so impressed. I see so many reviews on here complaining this broke them out or dried out their skin. What they may not know is that you WILL break out for the first few weeks that you are using any type of active ingredient. In fact, it means the product is working like it should. The salicylic acid is working hard to bring all that gunk underneath your skin to the surface, which ultimately results in fresh and healthy new skin. For the first three weeks I used this, I noticed tiny bumps all over my cheeks. In the weeks that followed, the bumps disappeared completely. I used to struggle with acne, and I truly believe this is the product that changed that for me. I no longer get breakouts, with the exception of the occasional pimple here and there. I have been consistently using this cleanser every single day, following it up with the Anua Heartleaf 77% toner, the Glow Recipe Watermelon Glow toner, and the Face Reality "clearderma" moisturizer, and my skin has never received as many compliments as it does now!
